title: A finite etale morphism is etale locally a finite disjoint union of copies of the base
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $x\in X$. Then there are an etale morphism $g:U\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a point $u\in U$ with $g(u)=x$, a finite set $J$ and a decomposition $Y\times_XU=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j$ of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $V_j$ such that, for every $j\in J$, the composite $V_j\hookrightarrow Y\times_XU\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}U$ is an isomorphism of schemes.

proof.text: *Etale localization to closed immersions.* $f$ is finite by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and etale, and an etale morphism is in particular unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-unramified-etale-local] to $f$ and $x$: there are an etale $g:U\to X$, a point $u\in U$ with $g(u)=x$, a finite set $J_0$ and pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $V_j\subseteq Y_U:=Y\times_XU$ ($j\in J_0$) covering $Y_U$, such that each $p_j:V_j\hookrightarrow Y_U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}U$ is a closed immersion. (The residue field condition of that lemma is not used.)

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04HN (line 1856): 'An etale morphism is unramified, hence we may apply Lemma 04HJ'

proof.text: *Each $p_j$ is an open and closed immersion.* The projection $\mathrm{pr}_2:Y_U\to U$ is the base change of the etale morphism $f$ along $g$, hence etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], clause 1, with $u:=g$ and $W:=Y$). The inclusion $V_j\hookrightarrow Y_U$ of an open subscheme is an open immersion, hence etale, and so the composite $p_j$ is etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], clauses (1) and (2)). Thus $p_j$ is an etale closed immersion, and by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-closed-immersion-open] it is an open immersion: its image $T_j:=p_j(V_j)$ is open and closed in $U$ and $p_j$ is an isomorphism of $V_j$ onto the open subscheme $T_j$ of $U$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Moreover $\mathrm{pr}_2(V_j)=T_j$.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04HL (line 1794): 'Now $V_{i,j}\to U$ is a closed immersion and etale. Hence it is an open immersion'; cited in the proof of Lemma 04HN

proof.text: *Shrinking $U$.* Let $J=\{j\in J_0: u\in T_j\}$ and $U'=\bigcap_{j\in J}T_j\setminus\bigcup_{j\in J_0\setminus J}T_j$ (with $\bigcap_{j\in\emptyset}T_j=U$). Since $J_0$ is finite and every $T_j$ is open and closed (step 2), $U'$ is a finite intersection of open subsets minus a finite union of closed subsets, hence open in $U$, and $u\in U'$ by the choice of $J$. Give $U'$ the open subscheme structure, with inclusion $\iota:U'\to U$, an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], hence etale; put $g'=g\circ\iota:U'\to X$, which is etale as a composite of etale morphisms ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], clauses (1) and (2)), and $g'(u)=g(u)=x$. By construction: $U'\subseteq T_j$ for $j\in J$ and $U'\cap T_j=\emptyset$ for $j\in J_0\setminus J$.

proof.text: *The base change to $U'$ is an open subscheme of $Y_U$.* Let $Y'=\mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(U')\subseteq Y_U$, an open subscheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (applied to $\mathrm{pr}_2:Y_U\to U$ and $\mathrm{id}_U$ over $U$, with the opens $Y_U$, $U'$ and $U$) the fibre product $Y_U\times_UU'$ is $Y'$, with projections the inclusion $Y'\hookrightarrow Y_U$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2|_{Y'}:Y'\to U'$. By the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], $(Y\times_XU)\times_UU'$ together with the composite $(Y\times_XU)\times_UU'\to Y\times_XU\to Y$ and the projection to $U'$ is a fibre product $Y\times_{X,g'}U'$: a pair of morphisms $a:T\to Y$, $b:T\to U'$ with $f\circ a=g'\circ b=g\circ(\iota\circ b)$ is the same as a morphism $(a,\iota\circ b):T\to Y_U$ together with $b$, compatible over $U$. Hence $Y\times_XU'=Y'$, with second projection $\mathrm{pr}_2|_{Y'}$.

proof.text: *The decomposition.* For $j\in J_0$ put $V'_j=V_j\cap Y'$, an open and closed subscheme of $Y'$ (intersection with $Y'$ of an open and closed subset of $Y_U$, with the open subscheme structure); the $V'_j$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $Y'$, because the $V_j$ do so in $Y_U$. If $j\notin J$ then $\mathrm{pr}_2(V_j)=T_j$ is disjoint from $U'$ (step 3), so $V'_j=\emptyset$; hence $Y'=\coprod_{j\in J}V'_j$. If $j\in J$ then $U'\subseteq T_j$ and $V'_j=p_j^{-1}(U')$; since $p_j:V_j\to T_j$ is an isomorphism of schemes (step 2), its restriction $V'_j=p_j^{-1}(U')\to U'$ to the open subscheme $U'$ of $T_j$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion], and it is the composite $V'_j\hookrightarrow Y'\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}U'$. With step 4 ($Y\times_XU'=Y'$) and step 3 ($g'$ etale, $g'(u)=x$, $J\subseteq J_0$ finite), $(g',u,J,(V'_j)_{j\in J})$ is as claimed. (If $Y_x=\emptyset$ then $J=\emptyset$ and $Y\times_XU'=\emptyset$, which is allowed.)

lean.statement: theorem finite_etale_etale_local_split {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f] [Etale f] (x : X) : ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (g : U ⟶ X) (u : U), Etale g ∧ g.base u = x ∧ ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → Scheme.{u}) (ι : ∀ j, V j ⟶ pullback f g), Finite J ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk (pullback f g) ι)) ∧ (∀ j, IsOpenImmersion (ι j) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (ι j)) ∧ (∀ j : J, ∃ e : V j ≅ U, e.hom = ι j ≫ pullback.snd f g)
